Insight1.summary: Astrocyte-derived fibronectin (FN1) is a proximal mechanistic mediator linking APOE ε4 to blood–brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease. APOE4 and amyloid-β42/inflammatory signals drive astrocytic FN1 upregulation and amorphous perivascular deposition that accumulates at AQP4-positive endfeet, and FN1 accumulation is sufficient to cause BBB leakage by engaging integrin/FAK signaling to suppress the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 trophic axis.
Insight1.how: This insight integrates postmortem human neuropathology, snRNA-seq, isogenic iPS cell-derived astrocyte and 3D vascular models, and zebrafish and APOE knock-in mouse studies. APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes showed elevated FN1 with amorphous (rather than fibrillar) deposits, and FN1 strongly colocalized with AQP4 at astrocytic endfeet at the gliovascular interface. Astroglial FN1 overexpression in zebrafish demonstrated sufficiency for BBB leakage (Extended Data Fig. 9b–e). Mechanistically, FN1 acts through integrin/FAK signaling to suppress VEGFA, which reduces endothelial HB-EGF and downstream astrocytic IGF-1; FAK inhibition, integrin β1 blockade (ATN-161), and HB-EGF/IGF-1 supplementation each restored components of this cascade and BBB integrity. Human CSF co-expression analyses (FN1 × APOE ε4 × disease interaction, F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴) provided clinical validation. The 71% AD risk reduction from an FN1 loss-of-function variant is attributed to prior work (ref. 12) cited as motivation, not a new finding of this paper.
Insight1.relevant:
Here we show that astrocyte-derived fibronectin (FN1) is a key mediator of apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4)-driven BBB dysfunction in AD. Using postmortem human brain tissue, human three-dimensional vascular models and in vivo models, we demonstrate that APOE4, amyloid-β42 and inflammatory signals induce astrocytic FN1 upregulation and excessive perivascular deposition. Fibronectin accumulation is sufficient to cause BBB leakage and disrupt VEGF/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling through integrin-mediated focal adhesion kinase activity. Reducing fibronectin or restoring growth factor signaling rescues BBB function in vitro and in vivo. Together, evidence from experimental models, human brain tissue and clinical datasets identifies fibronectin as a proximal mediator of APOE4-driven gliovascular dysfunction and highlights FN1 as a potential therapeutic target for vascular and BBB dysfunction in AD.

We previously reported that APOE ε4 carriers with AD accumulate fibronectin at the gliovascular interface of the BBB, and that a protective loss-of-function fibronectin 1 (FN1) variant reduces AD risk by 71% (ref. 12). These findings implicate fibronectin as a downstream mediator of APOE4 but leave its pathogenic mechanism unresolved.

APOE ε4/ε4 human astrocytes not only showed increased fibronectin expression but also generated amorphous fibronectin deposits. In contrast, APOE ε3/ε3 astrocytes deposited fibronectin at lower levels and in fibrillar, thread-like arrays.

These results demonstrate that, in the brain, astrocytes drive APOE ε4-dependent FN1 deposition at the vascular interface, consistent with their enrichment among FN1-expressing cells in perivascular regions.

FN1 strongly colocalized with AQP4 across all samples, confirming enrichment at astrocytic endfeet.

These findings indicate that the FN1/VEGF/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling axis regulates gliovascular homeostasis, which is disrupted in AD through APOE ε4-dependent elevated fibronectin deposition.

Our findings illustrate the crucial role of fibronectin as a pathological mediator in AD, especially among APOE ε4 carriers. Our work demonstrates that APOE ε4-induced BBB dysfunction in AD is augmented by the pathological deposition of fibronectin.

mcq_questions.question: In a study of Alzheimer's disease (AD), APOE ε4/ε4 human astrocytes showed elevated fibronectin (FN1) expression and generated amorphous FN1 deposits, whereas APOE ε3/ε3 astrocytes deposited lower levels of FN1 in fibrillar, thread-like arrays. FN1 strongly colocalized with AQP4 across all postmortem brain samples, confirming enrichment at astrocytic endfeet at the gliovascular interface. Based on these observations, which conclusion is best supported?

options.A: APOE ε4 carriers have higher perivascular FN1 at AQP4-positive endfeet than APOE ε3 carriers because the ε4 genotype shifts astrocyte FN1 deposition from a fibrillar to an amorphous pattern, which accumulates more readily at the gliovascular interface.
options.B: APOE ε4 carriers have higher perivascular FN1 at AQP4-positive endfeet because AQP4 expression drives FN1 transcription only in ε4 astrocytes, making the colocalization genotype-specific.
options.C: APOE ε3 carriers deposit FN1 predominantly at non-endfeet membrane domains, so the AQP4 colocalization seen in ε4 samples reflects a loss of ε3-specific AQP4 distribution rather than ε4-driven FN1 upregulation.
options.D: APOE ε4 carriers have higher perivascular FN1 because amorphous deposits indicate active proteolytic cleavage of fibrillar FN1, and the cleavage product binds AQP4 more avidly than intact FN1 fibrils.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The stem states that ε4/ε4 astrocytes show both higher FN1 expression and a shift to amorphous (rather than fibrillar) deposits, while FN1 colocalizes with AQP4 across all samples. Combining (i) ε4 = higher FN1 expression, (ii) ε4 = amorphous rather than fibrillar morphology, and (iii) colocalization with AQP4 at endfeet, the supported conclusion is that ε4 carriers accumulate more perivascular FN1 at AQP4-positive endfeet because the ε4 genotype shifts astrocytic FN1 to an amorphous pattern that accumulates at the gliovascular interface.

distractor_analysis.B: The reasoning fails: colocalization with AQP4 was observed across all samples (not only ε4), and the data do not support AQP4 driving FN1 transcription in an ε4-specific manner. The conclusion is not licensed.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion conflicts with the stated observations: FN1 colocalized with AQP4 across all samples, and lower FN1 in ε3 was paired with fibrillar arrays, not with loss of AQP4 distribution.
distractor_analysis.D: The reasoning invents a proteolytic mechanism not supported by any premise. The stem contrasts amorphous vs. fibrillar morphology but provides no evidence of proteolytic cleavage producing the amorphous form.

mcq_questions.question: In an AD model, astroglial FN1 overexpression in zebrafish was sufficient to cause BBB leakage. In vitro, FN1 acts through integrin/FAK signaling to suppress VEGFA, which reduces endothelial HB-EGF and downstream astrocytic IGF-1. FAK inhibition, integrin β1 blockade with ATN-161, and HB-EGF/IGF-1 supplementation each restored components of this cascade and BBB integrity. A human CSF analysis showed an FN1 × APOE ε4 × disease interaction (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). If astrocytic FN1 were experimentally reduced in APOE ε4 carriers with BBB leakage, what outcome does this evidence best predict?

options.B: BBB integrity would improve, because the zebrafish sufficiency test and the integrin/FAK rescue experiments together indicate that FN1 is a proximal driver whose reduction should restore VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling and barrier function.
options.A: BBB integrity would be unchanged, because the CSF interaction analysis only establishes that FN1 levels correlate with disease in ε4 carriers and cannot demonstrate that lowering FN1 is sufficient to restore barrier function.
options.C: BBB integrity would worsen, because amorphous FN1 deposits are protective and their loss would remove a stabilizing scaffold at AQP4-positive endfeet that compensates for ε4-related trophic deficits.
options.D: BBB integrity would improve only if FN1 were reduced below ε3 levels, because the ε4 phenotype is defined by amorphous (not fibrillar) FN1 and any residual ε4-pattern FN1 would continue to suppress VEGFA.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The zebrafish gain-of-function result shows FN1 is sufficient to cause BBB leakage. The integrin/FAK rescue experiments show that interrupting the FN1-initiated cascade restores BBB integrity, implying that lowering FN1 should relieve suppression of VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1. Chaining (i) FN1 overexpression is sufficient for leakage and (ii) blocking the downstream integrin/FAK node rescues barrier function predicts that reducing the proximal node (FN1) in ε4 carriers would likewise restore barrier function. The CSF interaction supports the clinical relevance of FN1 in ε4 AD but is not the sole basis.

distractor_analysis.A: The reasoning conflates an association (CSF interaction) with the experimental evidence: the zebrafish sufficiency and integrin/FAK rescue data directly show that interrupting the FN1-initiated cascade restores BBB integrity, so the counterfactual is answerable in the 'improve' direction.
distractor_analysis.C: The reasoning misreads amorphous FN1 deposits as protective; the stem states they are linked to APOE4-driven BBB dysfunction, and FN1 overexpression causes leakage, contradicting a protective role.
distractor_analysis.D: The conclusion overstates the quantitative threshold: no premise establishes that FN1 must be reduced below ε3 levels. The evidence shows amorphous, ε4-pattern FN1 is the pathogenic form, not that any residual ε4-pattern FN1 necessarily retains full suppressive activity.

Insight2.summary: In aged (21–22 month) APOE ε3/ε3 versus APOE ε4/ε4 knock-in mice, APOE ε4 drives a robust, genotype-dependent ~99% increase in vascular fibronectin (P = 4.1×10⁻³⁹), coinciding with elevated fibrinogen extravasation (+79.7%, P = 1.7×10⁻³), increased FN1–fibrinogen colocalization, and dextran–Texas Red leakage, collectively indicating APOE4-associated BBB dysfunction independent of overt amyloid pathology.
Insight2.how: The authors used aged APOE knock-in mice to isolate APOE4-dependent effects independent of AD pathology. Cortical sections were immunolabeled for FN1 and CD31, with FN1 intensity quantified across randomly selected vessels and statistical inference performed at the animal level using GEEs. Fibrinogen extravasation was assessed by confocal imaging and quantified with log-normal QQ plot validation, showing a +79.7% increase in APOE ε4 vessels, and FN1–fibrinogen colocalization was significantly elevated in APOE ε4 brains. A complementary dextran–Texas Red leakage assay confirmed increased BBB permeability. These orthogonal readouts collectively establish that APOE4 is associated with fibronectin-mediated BBB dysfunction (Fig. 1i–p, Extended Data Fig. 1e–h).
Insight2.relevant: To validate our results from human brains, we used aged (21- to 22-month-old) APOE ε3 and APOE ε4 knock-in mice, as APOE ε4 mice have previously been shown to exhibit CVP. APOE knock-in mice allowed us to isolate APOE4-dependent effects independent of overt AD pathology. We performed immunolabeling for fibronectin and CD31 in brain sections from both genotypes, followed by quantitative analyses of randomly selected regions of the cortex to evaluate the contribution of APOE ε4 to fibronectin accumulation. By comparing FN1 levels between genotypes using animals as the unit of inference, we found that APOE ε4 mouse brains showed markedly higher FN1 levels than APOE ε3 brains, with a percentage difference of +98.9% (95% confidence interval, 84.1–113.7%; P = 4.1 × 10⁻³⁹), indicating a robust genotype-dependent effect. Given that fibrinogen extravasation is an indication of BBB dysfunction, we assessed fibrinogen leakage in APOE ε4 versus APOE ε3 mouse brains to determine whether fibronectin accumulation correlates with this BBB compromise. APOE ε4 mouse brain tissue exhibited markedly elevated fibrinogen accumulation in the vasculature compared to APOE ε3 brains. A log-normal quantile–quantile (QQ) plot confirmed that fibrinogen intensity values followed a log-normal distribution, validating the use of parametric statistics. Quantitative analysis revealed a significant increase in fibrinogen intensity in vessels from APOE ε4 mouse brains relative to vessels from APOE ε3 brains. This genotype-dependent increase was consistently observed across individual mice. Furthermore, colocalization analysis showed that FN1 and fibrinogen overlap was significantly higher in APOE ε4 than in APOE ε3 mouse brains. Comparison of the dextran-based vessel leakage assay in control and APOE ε4 mouse brains (Extended Data Fig. 1e) showed significantly increased fibronectin deposition and dextran–Texas Red extravasation in APOE ε4 mice compared to control mice (Extended Data Fig. 1f–h), supporting the presence of a dysfunctional BBB and increased leakiness with elevated fibronectin levels in APOE ε4 mice.

Insight3.summary: Reactive astrocytes, particularly the SERPINA3⁺ inflammatory cluster 5, represent a major cellular source of APOE ε4-associated FN1 expression in AD brains. Although astrocytes constitute 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells (less than excitatory neurons at 32.68%), they appear to be the predominant contributors to pathological perivascular FN1 deposition at the gliovascular interface due to their abundance (~40% of brain cells), near-universal vascular contact, and demonstrated APOE ε4-dependent FN1 protein upregulation.
Insight3.how: The authors combined multiple lines of evidence: (1) snRNA-seq from 413,175 cells across 52 individuals showing astrocytes constitute 22.7% of 19,387 FN1-expressing cells; (2) ROSMAP analysis of 424 DLPFC samples (1.64 million nuclei) identifying astrocyte cluster 5 (SERPINA3⁺, inflammatory) as the cluster most strongly associated with FN1 in AD (β = 0.0300, FDR P = 1.55×10⁻⁶); (3) label transfer showing reactive astrocyte subcluster 5 expresses FN1 in the highest proportion of cells; (4) an independent snRNA-seq dataset showing astrocytes show the highest APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation; and (5) multiplex immunostaining of 1,098,338 cells demonstrating APOE ε4/ε4 selectively increases astrocytic FN1 protein. The authors argue that astrocyte predominance refers to pathological ECM deposition at the vascular interface, supported by their abundance and perivascular localization, rather than the proportion of total FN1-expressing cells.
Insight3.relevant: "We found that, among 413,175 cells sequenced, 19,387 cells express FN1 (4.7%), and astrocytes constitute 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells, while endothelial cells and pericytes together constitute 8.9% of FN1-expressing cells." "Astrocytes are among the most abundant CNS cell types, comprising ~40% of brain cells, and nearly all astrocytes contact the vasculature. In contrast, endothelial cells and pericytes together account for only 2–4% of CNS cells." "Fibronectin was associated with pathological AD, particularly in astrocyte cluster 5 (β: 0.0300, standard error (SE): 0.0057, false discovery rate (FDR) P: 1.55 × 10⁻⁶), characterized by inflammation, gliosis and SERPINA3 expression." "Label transfer from the ROSMAP snRNA-seq dataset to our independent snRNA-seq dataset further showed that reactive astrocyte subcluster 5 expressed FN1 in the highest proportion of cells, confirming that reactive astrocytes are a major source of FN1." "We analyzed an independent human single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) dataset and found that astrocytes show the highest upregulation of FN1 with APOE ε4." "Automated analyses of 1,098,338 cells (165,099 GFAP+ astrocytes, 417,936 MBP+ oligodendrocytes, 153,096 IBA1+ microglia, 205,398 MAP2+ neurons, 86,668 CD31+ endothelial cells and 70,141 PDGFRβ+ pericytes) showed that the APOE ε4/ε4 genotype increases FN1 protein levels in astrocytes." "Although single-cell transcriptomic studies have reported higher FN1 expression in pericytes and endothelial cells than in astrocytes, these measurements reflect mRNA abundance rather than extracellular protein deposition, which can diverge substantially due to post-transcriptional regulation and ECM assembly." "Although we found that FN1 is produced by multiple cell types, consistent with previous studies, the combination of astrocyte abundance at the gliovascular niche and marked APOE ε4-associated upregulation of FN1 suggests that astrocytes are the predominant contributors to pathological fibronectin deposition in AD."

mcq_questions.question: In a single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis of 413,175 cells from 52 individuals, 19,387 cells (4.7%) express FN1. Astrocytes constitute 22.7% of these FN1-expressing cells, whereas excitatory neurons constitute 32.68% and endothelial cells plus pericytes together constitute 8.9%. Astrocytes are ~40% of brain cells and nearly all contact vasculature, whereas endothelial cells and pericytes together are only 2–4% of CNS cells. ROSMAP analysis of 424 DLPFC samples (1.64 million nuclei) links FN1 to astrocyte cluster 5 (SERPINA3⁺, β = 0.0300, FDR P = 1.55×10⁻⁶). Which interpretation is best supported?

options.B: Excitatory neurons are the predominant source of pathological perivascular FN1 deposition in AD because they account for the largest fraction (32.68%) of FN1-expressing cells in the snRNA-seq data.
options.C: Astrocytes are likely the predominant contributors to pathological perivascular FN1 deposition in AD because, although they are 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells, their abundance (~40% of brain cells) and near-universal vascular contact indicate a disproportionate role at the gliovascular interface.
options.A: Endothelial cells and pericytes are the predominant contributors to pathological perivascular FN1 deposition in AD because they jointly constitute only 8.9% of FN1-expressing cells, indicating highly cell-type-specific expression.
options.D: No cell type can be considered predominant because astrocytes, excitatory neurons, endothelial cells, and pericytes all express FN1, and the fractions are all within the same order of magnitude.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option (A) correctly integrates the stated observations: astrocytes are 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells (lower than excitatory neurons at 32.68%), but their overall abundance (~40% of brain cells), near-universal vascular contact, and strong AD association in cluster 5 (β = 0.0300, FDR P = 1.55×10⁻⁶) together support their predominance at the perivascular ECM interface, not their numerical majority among FN1-expressing cells.

distractor_analysis.B: Right observation (excitatory neurons are the largest fraction of FN1-expressing cells at 32.68%), but wrong conclusion: the question requires integrating cell abundance and perivascular localization, not just the fraction of FN1-expressing cells.
distractor_analysis.C: Right observation (astrocytes are ~40% of brain cells and contact vasculature), but wrong conclusion: a low fraction among FN1-expressing cells does not, on its own, indicate a 'highly cell-type-specific' pattern, and the 8.9% figure does not support endothelial/pericyte predominance.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion: the convergence of multiple independent lines (cluster 5 association, perivascular localization, cell abundance, APOE ε4-dependent upregulation) does license a predominant contributor even when no single cell type is a majority of FN1-expressing cells.

mcq_questions.question: Multiplex immunostaining of 1,098,338 cells across genotypes shows that the APOE ε4/ε4 genotype increases FN1 protein levels selectively in astrocytes (165,099 GFAP⁺ astrocytes analyzed). An independent snRNA-seq dataset shows astrocytes display the highest APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation among all cell types. Single-cell transcriptomic studies have reported higher FN1 mRNA in pericytes and endothelial cells than in astrocytes. Given these findings, what is the strongest conclusion about astrocytic FN1 in AD?

options.A: Astrocytes do not contribute meaningfully to FN1 production in AD because single-cell transcriptomic studies show higher FN1 mRNA in pericytes and endothelial cells than in astrocytes.
options.B: Astrocytes contribute substantially to APOE ε4-associated pathological FN1 deposition in AD because the APOE ε4/ε4 genotype selectively upregulates astrocytic FN1 protein and astrocytes show the highest APOE ε4-dependent FN1 mRNA upregulation, even though mRNA measurements underestimate astrocytic ECM protein output.
options.C: Pericytes and endothelial cells are the dominant source of pathological FN1 deposition in AD because their mRNA levels exceed those in astrocytes, and mRNA abundance is the primary determinant of ECM protein levels.
options.D: The APOE ε4/ε4 genotype increases FN1 protein in all CNS cell types equally because the immunostaining panel included astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, neurons, endothelial cells, and pericytes.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option (B) integrates: (1) APOE ε4/ε4 selectively increases astrocytic FN1 protein (immunostaining), (2) astrocytes show the highest APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation (independent snRNA-seq), and (3) mRNA levels and ECM protein deposition can diverge due to post-transcriptional regulation and ECM assembly, which resolves the apparent contradiction with prior single-cell mRNA studies.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion: ignores the stated evidence that APOE ε4/ε4 selectively increases astrocytic FN1 protein and that astrocytes show the highest ε4-dependent upregulation, and the explicit caveat that mRNA and ECM protein can diverge.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion: assumes mRNA abundance is the primary determinant of ECM protein levels, contradicting the stated caveat that mRNA and deposited ECM protein can diverge substantially.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion: the stated finding is that the APOE ε4/ε4 effect is selective for astrocytes, not equal across all cell types.

Insight5.summary: APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes show 163.6% higher APOE protein signal (P = 1.6 × 10⁻²¹) and stronger APOE–FN1 colocalization (R² = 0.396 vs 0.049 in ε3/ε3), with postmortem ε4/ε4 AD brains confirming elevated APOE (+64.9%) and FN1 (+30.6%). Co-immunoprecipitation of FN1 from astrocyte media and lysates failed to detect direct APOE binding. The authors attribute the elevated APOE signal in ε4/ε4 to perivascular retention from impaired lipidation/secretion rather than increased synthesis, and identify astrocytes as the predominant source of pathological FN1 deposition.

Insight9.summary: The VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling axis shows evolutionarily conserved reductions across zebrafish, APP knock-in mice, and human AD brains (Braak V–VI), with highly significant decreases in all three growth factors. In zebrafish, VEGFR inhibition compromises tight junction integrity (reduced ZO-1/GFP colocalization), which is rescued by HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment, while human genetic and transcriptomic data provide associative validation linking fibronectin to disrupted VEGF/IGF-1 signaling.
Insight9.how: The authors performed immunostaining and quantification of VEGFA, HB-EGF, and IGF-1 across three species (zebrafish, APP knock-in mice, and human Braak I vs. Braak VI brains), reporting highly significant reductions in AD models (Welch's t test, P < 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ for HB-EGF/IGF-1; P = 9.7 × 10⁻⁸ for VEGFA in human tissue). In zebrafish, VEGFR inhibition reduced ZO-1/GFP colocalization in parenchymal capillaries, and HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment restored tight junction levels — the only direct functional rescue demonstration in the paper. KEGG analysis of FN1×APOE4 interaction genes from ROSMAP brain endothelial scRNA-seq identified insulin signaling among negatively regulated pathways. An mQTL (rs2304573) linked an intronic FN1 variant to altered VEGFA methylation, which the authors describe as supporting but not proving transcriptional regulation of VEGFA by fibronectin.

options.A: These reductions show the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 axis is evolutionarily conserved and consistently suppressed in AD-like pathology, because the same direction of change was observed across zebrafish, mouse, and human tissue with high statistical significance.
options.B: The identical P-values across zebrafish, mice, and humans indicate the magnitude of VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 loss is the same in each species, because shared significance levels imply shared effect sizes.
options.C: The reductions prove that fibronectin is the obligatory upstream driver of VEGFA loss, because the most significant P-values identify the most upstream step in the cascade.
options.D: The reductions rule out any compensatory upregulation of these growth factors in AD brains, because a significant decrease at one time point excludes all homeostatic responses.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A correctly combines two stated premises: (1) the same direction of change (reduction) across zebrafish, APP knock-in mice, and human Braak V–VI brains, and (2) highly significant P-values in all three species. Together these support the conclusion that suppression of the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 axis is a conserved feature of AD-like pathology. The conclusion (conserved suppression) and the reasoning (cross-species concordance plus statistical significance) are both warranted.

distractor_analysis.B: Fails on reasoning. Shared significance (P-values passing a threshold) does not imply shared effect size; P-values reflect effect size, variance, and sample size together. Two P-values of similar magnitude can correspond to very different biological effect sizes, so the magnitude of loss is not established to be identical.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on reasoning. Statistical significance (small P-value) does not identify upstream versus downstream position in a pathway. The stem does not establish fibronectin as the obligatory driver; the paper describes the FN1–VEGFA methylation link only as supportive of transcriptional regulation, not as a necessity test.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on reasoning. A significant decrease at one stage does not exclude compensatory upregulation at other stages or in other cell types; the measurement is a snapshot and cannot rule out homeostatic responses the assay did not capture.

mcq_questions.question: In zebrafish parenchymal capillaries, VEGFR inhibition significantly reduced ZO-1/GFP colocalization (a tight-junction integrity readout), and co-treatment with HB-EGF and IGF-1 restored ZO-1/GFP levels. Which conclusion is best licensed by these combined observations?

options.B: HB-EGF and IGF-1 treatment is sufficient to rescue VEGFR-inhibition-induced tight-junction disruption in parenchymal capillaries, and the FN1/VEGFA methylation link provides associative support consistent with fibronectin contributing to VEGFA regulation; insulin signaling downregulation in the FN1×APOE4 set parallels the IGF-1 axis loss observed in AD tissue.

options.C: The FN1 mQTL proves fibronectin is the unique obligatory transcriptional repressor of VEGFA in human AD, because a single intronic variant linked to methylation establishes causality and excludes all other regulators.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A chains three stated observations correctly: (1) the rescue experiment shows HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment is sufficient to restore ZO-1/GFP colocalization after VEGFR inhibition — the correct inference is sufficiency in that context, not necessity or uniqueness; (2) the FN1 mQTL is correctly characterized as associative support for fibronectin contributing to VEGFA regulation, consistent with the paper's cautious wording; (3) insulin signaling being negatively regulated in the FN1×APOE4 gene set parallels the IGF-1 axis reduction seen in vivo. All three premises are linked to the conclusion without overreach.

distractor_analysis.A: Fails on reasoning. A rescue experiment demonstrates that a manipulation is sufficient to restore a phenotype, not that the inhibited component is unnecessary. The baseline (without VEGFR inhibition) was not compared to the rescue condition in the stem, so VEGFR's physiological role is not negated by the rescue.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on reasoning. A single mQTL linking an intronic FN1 variant to VEGFA methylation is associative evidence consistent with transcriptional regulation; it does not establish fibronectin as the unique obligatory repressor, nor does it exclude other regulators.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on reasoning. Rescue by two ligands shows that supplying those ligands can compensate; it does not prove the defect arises solely from loss of those ligands, nor does it exclude other downstream consequences of VEGFR inhibition. The conclusion 'must arise solely' oversteps the evidence.

Insight10.summary: CSF fibronectin (FN1) levels are significantly elevated in AD (t = 5.22, P = 3.31×10⁻⁷), and FN1–VEGFA coexpression in CSF shows a significant three-way interaction with APOE ε4 status and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴), with non-ε4 AD cases exhibiting a compensatory VEGFA increase that is absent in ε4 carriers. This CNS-specific relationship (absent in plasma, r = 0.13) supports FN1 as both a biomarker candidate and a mechanistic mediator of AD-related BBB dysfunction.
Insight10.how: The authors quantified FN1 protein in CSF from the Emory Somalogic 7k dataset (n = 156 AD, n = 139 controls) and reported significantly elevated AD levels (Fig. 2f). Transformed gene coexpression analyses revealed that FN1 strongly predicts VEGFA (F = 26.39, P = 2.79×10⁻⁷) with a significant three-way interaction among FN1, APOE ε4 status, and disease status (Fig. 5n). Stratified visualization showed compensatory VEGFA elevation in AD confined to non-ε4 carriers. Plasma analysis (n = 113) showed no FN1–VEGFA correlation (Pearson r = 0.13, R² = 0.018), confirming CNS specificity. The Discussion integrates these findings to position FN1 as both a biomarker candidate and a mechanistic mediator of AD-related BBB dysfunction.
Insight10.relevant: Consistent with the increased fibronectin deposition observed in APOE ε4/ε4 cellular and vascular models, we also found that FN1 protein levels were significantly elevated in the CSF of individuals with AD compared to controls (Student's t test: t = 5.22, P = 3.31 × 10⁻⁷). FN1 expression was strongly associated with VEGFA levels (F = 26.39, P = 2.79 × 10⁻⁷), and a significant three-way interaction among FN1, APOE ε4 status and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81 × 10⁻⁴) indicated that the slope of the FN1–VEGFA relationship differs in APOE ε4 carriers with AD compared to noncarriers and controls. In controls, VEGFA expression levels were similar between APOE ε3 and APOE ε4 carriers, whereas in AD brains, non-ε4 carriers exhibited a compensatory increase that was absent in APOE ε4 carriers. Unlike in CSF, plasma FN1 did not correlate with VEGFA (Pearson r = 0.13; R² = 0.018), indicating that the FN1–VEGFA association is CNS-specific and varies according to the APOE genotype in AD. This conclusion is supported by elevated FN1 levels in the CSF of living individuals with AD, the strong association between fibronectin and inflammatory astrocytic states in human AD brains, and altered VEGFA regulation associated with FN1 variants in postmortem AD brains, highlighting FN1 as both a biomarker candidate and a mechanistic mediator of AD-related BBB dysfunction.

mcq_questions.question: In CSF from 156 AD and 139 control individuals, FN1 protein was significantly elevated in AD (t = 5.22, P = 3.31×10⁻⁷), and FN1–VEGFA coexpression showed a three-way interaction with APOE ε4 and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). In plasma from 113 individuals, FN1 and VEGFA did not correlate (Pearson r = 0.13, R² = 0.018). Which comparison best captures what these observations establish about the FN1–VEGFA relationship?

options.A: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is detectable in plasma but absent in CSF, because plasma measurements reflect systemic fibronectin more reliably than lumbar CSF does.
options.C: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is detectable in CSF but not plasma, and its CSF slope differs by APOE ε4 status in AD, indicating a CNS-specific, genotype-modulated association.
options.B: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is detectable in both CSF and plasma with similar magnitudes, because r = 0.13 is comparable to F = 26.39 once converted to a correlation.
options.D: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is detectable only in AD carriers of APOE ε4, because the three-way F statistic shows that APOE ε4 status is required for the association to exist.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B correctly integrates three premises from the stem: (1) FN1 and VEGFA correlate in CSF (shown by F = 26.39 and the three-way interaction F = 14.02 indicating the slope depends on APOE ε4 status and disease status), (2) they do not correlate in plasma (Pearson r = 0.13, R² = 0.018), and (3) the CSF relationship is modulated by APOE ε4 in AD. Combining these yields that the FN1–VEGFA association is CNS-specific and genotype-modulated.

distractor_analysis.A: Reverses the direction of the cross-tissue comparison; the data show absence in plasma and presence in CSF, not the reverse. This is a naive single-premise reading of one statistic (plasma r) taken out of context.
distractor_analysis.B: Falsely equates an F statistic from an ANOVA-like model (F = 26.39) with a Pearson correlation (r = 0.13); these are different statistic types and cannot be compared in magnitude. The rubric for evidential validity explicitly forbids cross-statistic comparisons.
distractor_analysis.D: Overstates APOE ε4 status as a prerequisite; the three-way interaction shows the slope DIFFERS by ε4 status (the association is present in both groups but with different patterns, with non-ε4 AD showing a compensatory VEGFA rise). Sufficiency/modulation is misread as necessity.

mcq_questions.question: CSF FN1 is elevated in AD (t = 5.22, P = 3.31×10⁻⁷) and shows a three-way interaction with VEGFA, APOE ε4, and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). In AD, non-ε4 carriers exhibit a compensatory VEGFA increase that ε4 carriers lack, while plasma shows no FN1–VEGFA correlation (r = 0.13). If the FN1–VEGFA coexpression signal were driven primarily by a systemic inflammatory response leaking into CSF rather than a CNS process, which finding above would be contradicted, and why?

options.A: The plasma r = 0.13 would be contradicted, because a systemic driver should produce a measurable plasma correlation unless plasma sampling is unreliable, and the CSF three-way interaction would remain consistent with leakage.
options.D: The CSF-only FN1–VEGFA association (strong in CSF, absent in plasma) combined with the APOE-ε4-dependent slope in AD would be contradicted, because systemic leakage would not be expected to be absent in plasma yet present in CSF nor to depend on APOE ε4 status.
options.B: The AD elevation of FN1 (t = 5.22) would be contradicted, because a systemic driver should equally elevate FN1 in controls, making the AD-versus-control difference impossible to explain.
options.C: The F = 14.02 three-way interaction would be contradicted, because a systemic driver would produce a main effect of disease only, and any interaction involving APOE ε4 would indicate a CNS-specific pathway.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B identifies the pattern that a systemic-leakage hypothesis cannot explain: (1) the dissociation between CSF (strong FN1–VEGFA signal) and plasma (no correlation, r = 0.13), and (2) the APOE-ε4-dependent slope of the FN1–VEGFA relationship specifically in AD. A systemic process should affect both compartments and would not be expected to produce an APOE-ε4-by-disease interaction in CSF alone. The counterfactual therefore licenses rejecting the systemic-leakage interpretation.

distractor_analysis.A: Partially correct that plasma r = 0.13 is inconsistent with strong systemic drive, but wrong to claim the three-way interaction would remain consistent; an interaction involving APOE ε4 status is hard to attribute to non-specific systemic leakage. The reasoning is incomplete.
distractor_analysis.B: Misidentifies which observation is contradicted; the AD-versus-control FN1 elevation (t = 5.22) is itself a CNS-specific datum from CSF and would not be falsified by a systemic-leakage model that elevates FN1 broadly — the elevation in CSF could still occur. The reasoning applies a wrong premise.
distractor_analysis.C: Partially correct that a pure systemic driver would not generate an APOE-ε4-by-disease interaction, but the option inverts the logic: it claims the interaction would be contradicted, whereas in fact the interaction is the very finding that argues against a systemic-only explanation. The conclusion sign is reversed.
